title: New XFS volumes may not mount on nodes with older kernels (xfsprogs nrext64; Amazon Linux 2) — set legacyXFS

detection.reason: StorageClass fstype and node kernel versions are not collected yet (Storage tab slice); the hint names nodes whose OS image ships an older kernel

quote: **As a result, newly formatted XFS volumes may fail to mount on nodes with older kernel versions.**
remediation: On clusters with XFS StorageClasses (csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: xfs) and nodes on older kernels — upstream names Amazon Linux 2; the nrext64 feature needs Linux 5.19 or newer, so AL2 (4.14/5.10), Ubuntu 20.04/22.04 GA kernels and Bottlerocket on 5.10/5.15 are affected — set legacy XFS formatting before upgrading: EKS add-on / Helm node.legacyXFS=true, flag --legacy-xfs on the node plugin. It also disables nrext64 only in v1.49.1, v1.50.1 and v1.51.0 or newer (not v1.49.0 / v1.50.0), so target one of those. Otherwise new XFS volumes are formatted with nrext64 and fail to mount on those nodes. The setting affects only volumes formatted after it is enabled: volumes already formatted by v1.49.0 / v1.50.0 must be re-created. Moving the nodes to a newer kernel (AL2023) removes the need.
verifyCommand: kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.name): \(.status.nodeInfo.osImage) kernel \(.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion)"'; kubectl get storageclass -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.provisioner == "ebs.csi.aws.com") | "\(.metadata.name): \(.parameters // {} | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(" "))"'  # a node kernel older than 5.19 plus fstype=xfs (csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype) on a CSI StorageClass needs legacyXFS
coversNotes: URGENT (1.50.0): A workaround is available in v1.50.1 and later.
URGENT (1.50.1): A workaround is available via the --legacy-xfs and node.legacyXFS parameters, see the full
Setting legacyXFS to true now disables nrext64.

title: v1.50.0/v1.50.1 break throughput handling — skip to v1.50.2 or later

detection.reason: read from the image TAG of the ebs-csi-controller / ebs-csi-node workloads — a digest-pinned image (@sha256:…) or a mirror that renames the tag is not resolved and reads clean

quote: **WARNING: This version contains a bug that breaks handling of throughput. It is strongly recommended to skip directly to `v1.50.2` or later.**
remediation: This release mishandles StorageClass throughput: volumes can be created without the throughput you asked for. Upgrade straight past it (to the target version); if the cluster runs it now, re-check gp3 volumes created while it ran (aws ec2 describe-volumes --query 'Volumes[].[VolumeId,Throughput]').
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^ebs-csi-(controller|node(-.+)?)$")) | .metadata.namespace as $n | .metadata.name as $w | .spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "ebs-plugin") | "\($n)/\($w): \(.image)"'  # a tag of v1.50.0 or v1.50.1 is the affected build

title: gp3 IOPS are no longer clamped at 16,000 — StorageClasses relying on the clamp now provision more IOPS

detection.reason: StorageClass parameters are not collected yet (Storage tab slice); the hint names the EBS CSI StorageClasses

quote: Retrieve maximum IOPS limit dynamically via `CreateVolume` dry-run to support increased IOPS limits for GP3 and other volume types
remediation: StorageClasses that size IOPS from capacity (iopsPerGB, with allowAutoIOPSPerGBIncrease) or request more IOPS than the old clamp now provision more IOPS — and cost more — than before the upgrade: v1.44 raised the io2 IOPS:GiB ratio from 500:1 to 1000:1, v1.47 the io2 total cap from 64,000 to 256,000 (Block Express), and v1.50 replaced gp3's fixed 16,000 cap with the limit EC2 reports. Set an explicit iops (and throughput) on those StorageClasses to keep today's cost.
verifyCommand: kubectl get storageclass -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.provisioner == "ebs.csi.aws.com") | "\(.metadata.name): \(.parameters // {} | to_entries | map("\(.key)=\(.value)") | join(" "))"'  # type=gp3 with iopsPerGB, or iops above 16000, now provisions up to the EC2-reported maximum
